meta.description: Analyzes pooled CRISPR screens with MAGeCK (Li et al 2014), covering count generation, the RRA two-condition workflow, the MLE multi-condition workflow, normalization choice, sgRNA efficiency injection, paired-sample testing, time-course design, drug-screen design matrices, MAGeCKFlute and MAGeCK-VISPR downstream visualization, and decision logic for MAGeCK vs JACKS/BAGEL2/drugZ/Chronos.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/results in the Skill; Input 7 confirmed the natural response refuses to fabricate FDR/LFC values without real data.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 confirmed the Skill's content stays confined to pooled-screen statistics; nothing pushes toward patient-level diagnosis or prescription, and no such conclusion was produced.

methodological_ground.detail: RRA/MLE decision tree, normalization mechanism, and correction guidance all matched real, independently-verified behavior (e.g. PR-AUC 0.993 vs CEGv2/NEGv1 on real HAP1 data).

code_usability.detail: Core CLI + design-matrix + Python analysis code (time_course_consistency) is fully runnable and produced ground-truth-correct results on real and synthetic data across 5 executed inputs. Two secondary visualization snippets (volcano() missing an import; FluteRRA failing against the real MAGeCK/MAGeCKFlute build) are diagnosable, fixable bugs in example code, not the central hit-calling operation, scored as Correctness/P1-P2 findings rather than a veto.

functional_suitability.note: Covers count/test/mle/normalization/efficiency/time-course/drug-screen/visualization/Flute/VISPR/reconciliation comprehensively (4/4 Completeness), decision tree and CLI flags verified accurate against the real installed MAGeCK 0.5.9.5 (3/4 Correctness — docked for the FluteRRA/volcano() bugs and missing --permutation-round guidance found during execution), approach well-matched to the task (4/4 Appropriateness).

reliability.note: Failure Modes section (NaN beta, all-significant RRA, batch absorption, efficiency mismatch) gives explicit trigger/mechanism/fix structure (3/4 Fault Tolerance -- misses the permutation-round/wald-fdr edge case found in Input 5), Common Errors table is specific and actionable (3/4 Error Reporting), fixes are concrete and correctly scoped per the Category-3 Scene Override (4/4 Recoverability).

performance_context.note: usage-guide.md and examples/ separated from SKILL.md for progressive disclosure (3/4 Token Cost); clear linear reading order (count -> qc -> test/mle -> Flute -> pathway) with no redundant steps (4/4 Execution Efficiency).

agent_usability.note: Decision tree and algorithm walkthroughs are immediately actionable (4/4 Learnability); consistent terminology across SKILL.md and usage-guide.md (4/4 Consistency); output columns explicitly enumerated for both RRA and MLE (4/4 Feedback Design); strong but not complete pitfall coverage -- misses the permutation-round granularity issue and FluteRRA's proj/outdir requirement (3/4 Error Prevention).

human_usability.note: Quick Start prompts match natural researcher phrasing (4/4 Discoverability); handles starting mid-pipeline (count table in hand, no FASTQ) gracefully but doesn't say so explicitly (3/4 Forgiveness, scored per the Category-3 override -- strict validation is not penalized).

security.note: No hardcoded secrets, no unsanitized string execution, CLI flag construction only; no sensitive data handling concerns for screen count data.

maintainability.note: Clean separation across SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples/ (4/4 Modularity); thresholds and tables are independently updatable (3/4 Modifiability); Quantitative Thresholds table gives objective, independently-verifiable pass/fail criteria, confirmed against real data in this audit (4/4 Testability).

agent_specific.note: Long, specific description with low false-trigger risk (4/4 Trigger Precision); SKILL.md is thorough but table-heavy, usage-guide.md separated (3/4 Progressive Disclosure); 8 cross-referenced Related Skills with clean integration points (4/4 Composability); CLI point estimates fully reproducible across reruns but permutation-based FDR granularity is sensitive to design changes at MAGeCK's own default, undocumented (3/4 Idempotency); Failure Modes/Common Errors act as partial escape hatches but there is no explicit human-handoff or out-of-scope guidance, e.g. for clinical-boundary-adjacent requests (3/4 Escape Hatches).

key_strengths: mageck test (RRA), run on real public HAP1 TKOv3 data, reproduced published essential-gene biology exactly: PR-AUC 0.993 vs CEGv2/NEGv1, clearing the Skill's own >0.7 threshold, and identical top-10 hits on an independent rerun.

The MLE design-matrix pattern and the bundled time_course_consistency() function correctly recovered 100% of planted synthetic hits (20/20) with zero false positives across a 50-gene time-course test.

CLI flag documentation was verified accurate against the real installed MAGeCK 0.5.9.5 (--sgrna-efficiency scoped to mle only, --gene-lfc-method choices, --norm-method control requiring --control-sgrna, etc.).

Failure Modes and Normalization Decision tables give specific, actionable guidance that matched real diagnosed behavior when tested (control normalization recovering 0%->100% recall of masked hits under heavy selection).

recommendations.title: MLE permutation-FDR is undocumented-sensitive to --permutation-round and covariate set
recommendations.problem: Adding a batch covariate to an otherwise-identical MLE design flipped 15/15 significant genes to 0/15, purely from mageck mle's own default --permutation-round=2 producing a p-value floor that straddles the BH 0.05 line; wald-fdr stayed robustly significant throughout.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's MLE section and worked examples never mention --permutation-round or give guidance on when to trust wald-fdr over the coarser permutation-based fdr column.
recommendations.fix: Add a note to the MLE section recommending --permutation-round >= 10 (matching mageck mle --help's own suggestion) for any design used to draw conclusions, and to cross-check wald-fdr when the primary fdr sits near a threshold.

recommendations.title: MAGeCKFlute FluteRRA example fails as documented against real MAGeCK output
recommendations.problem: Running the exact FluteRRA(...) call shown in SKILL.md against real mageck test output fails to create its own output subdirectory, and after that is fixed manually, fails again with 'undefined columns selected'.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's example omits the proj= argument that names the output subdirectory (which FluteRRA does not auto-create), and its Version Compatibility note ('MAGeCKFlute 2.0+') does not anticipate the unreleased GitHub-HEAD build's deeper column-handling behavior.
recommendations.fix: Add proj= to the documented example, note that the MAGeCKFlute_<proj>/ output directory must exist before calling FluteRRA, and add the remaining column error to the Common Errors table as a known MAGeCKFlute compatibility gap pending upstream investigation.

recommendations.title: No platform caveat or fallback for mageck-vispr
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md documents mageck-vispr init / snakemake / vispr server with no mention that this stack is Linux/Mac-only (Snakemake+Flask, no Windows/PyPI build), and no pointer to a fallback.
recommendations.root_cause: The VISPR section was written without a cross-platform caveat, and its Related Skills link to screen-qc is not connected to this specific failure case.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note that mageck-vispr requires Linux/Mac and that screen-qc's pandas/matplotlib QC covers the same numbers as a Windows-compatible fallback.

recommendations.title: volcano() Python snippet is missing an import
recommendations.problem: The documented volcano() function calls pd.read_csv but only imports matplotlib.pyplot and numpy, so it raises NameError if copy-pasted verbatim.
recommendations.root_cause: A one-line omission in the code snippet.
recommendations.fix: Add 'import pandas as pd' to the snippet's import block.

recommendations.title: 'Every gene appears significant' overstates the heavy-selection failure mode
recommendations.problem: At a realistic screen scale, heavy selection (45% guides changing) under median normalization did not make every gene significant; it collapsed recall of one selection direction to 0% while leaving the other direction largely correct.
recommendations.root_cause: The Failure Modes section describes only the 'everything significant' extreme, not the direction-specific masking that this audit's real test actually produced.
recommendations.fix: Rephrase the symptom to cover both possible manifestations: universal significance in some cases, or asymmetric recall collapse (one direction of true hits disappearing) in others -- both fixed the same way (switch to control normalization).

recommendations.title: No explicit anti-fabrication instruction
recommendations.problem: Nothing in SKILL.md explicitly instructs against reporting FDR/LFC/beta values without having actually run mageck; the correct refusal behavior currently relies entirely on general model norms.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's failure-mode and error-handling sections cover technical MAGeCK failures but not the request-level case of a user asking for invented numbers.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line instruction: never report FDR/LFC/beta values without having actually run mageck count/test/mle on the user's own data.
